biography.plain_text: Harold Zeigler is an American motor dealer who founded Zeigler Auto Group in Michigan. He bought its first Ford dealership in Lowell in 1975 and expanded into other franchises. The family business grew across the Midwest; his son Aaron became president, while Harold retained the chairmanship after stepping back from daily management.

long_biography.plain_text:
Harold Zeigler began Drive for Life, a charity event that became a fixture of Kalamazoo's fundraising calendar. The motor dealer's initiative has supported the American Cancer Society and local organisations, including the First Day Shoe Fund. His family and the dealership group have continued to organise and support the gala.

Before establishing his business, Zeigler worked in his father's trailer and motorhome trade and held other jobs to pay for college. He transferred to Central Michigan University to be near Bonnie, whom he had met through her brother. They married while still students.
